newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tan Chong jumps in Singapore on requote.
newsitem.headline: Tan Chong jumps in Singapore on requote.

text.p: Malaysian motor group Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd rose sharply at the start of trading on Thursday on the Singapore bourse on requotation of its shares after being suspended since November 22.
At 0110 GMT, the stock which is traded in the over the counter market in Singapore, jumped over six percent, or by Singapore S$0.18 to S$2.83 on 2.7 million shares.
Tan Chong announced last Friday a scheme to spin off three of its divisions for separate listings.
Its operations would be divided into four divisions - motor and truck assembly, autoparts and manufacturing, non-motor division and foreign operations.
The motor division would be retained under Tan Chong, which assembles Nissan cars.

Tan Chong said it would apply for the listing of the autoparts and non-motor divisions on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and the foreign division on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.
"The market is taking the news of the spinoff well," said an institutional dealer in Singapore.
"Existing shareholders will get some shares in the three companies. The move shows Tan Chong is putting better focus on its businesses. Overall, it is good for investors," he said.
Dealers said they expected Tan Chong shares to rally when trading starts on the Malaysian bourse at 0130 GMT.
